display.title: Episode 307: The Flickering Flame (Zos Chanukah)
display.summary_short: On the night all eight Chanukah lights are lit: what the candles whisper about Moshiach's clouds, a first-grade siddur celebration in Studio 604, and Rabbi Yisrael Salanter's lesson from a cobbler's lamp.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on the eighth night of Chanukah 5748. Uncle Yossi shares the Rebbe's call, in the name of the Frierdiker Rebbe, to listen to what the Chanukah lights are telling us: a message of emunah and bitachon that the King of miracles will soon bring Moshiach, who will gather all Jews on heavenly clouds, as the prophet Daniel says, to Eretz Yisroel and the rebuilt Beis HaMikdash. 'Ad mosai? We want Moshiach now!' After the Hakochainik march, a first-grade class from a Boro Park girls' school, which has just received its first siddurim, visits the studio with its teacher, sings a song about the siddur, and leads the Shema; Uncle Yossi calls the siddur a telephone to Hashem. Story time tells 'The Flickering Flame': collecting tzedakah late at night, Rabbi Yisrael of Salant finds a cobbler still working by his lamp. The cobbler explains his rule, 'as long as the candle burns, one can still repair', and the rabbi exclaims that this is a lesson for life: as long as the neshamah is within us, we can still do teshuvah. The show ends with Shabbos candle time.
display.lesson: As long as the candle is burning, we can still repair: as long as we are alive, we can always do teshuvah and improve.

date.note: 'Tonight is Zos Chanukah... we light all eight candles' (8th candle on the night of 22 Dec 1987); Shabbos candles 'this coming Friday, December 25th' at 4:16. Matches the weekly estimate.

privacy.note: A first-grade teacher and her school's dean are named on air; the children are not named.

sources_cited.ref: 'Listen carefully to what the candles are saying'
sources_cited.note: Cited as the Rebbe quoting the Frierdiker Rebbe.
'With the clouds of heaven': the clouds that will bring the Jews home.
Thanking Hashem for miracles and wonders.
'The steps of a man are established by Hashem', quoted as a teaching of the Baal Shem Tov.
